post.summary:
Receives one signed feedback event of an email provider. The destination's manifest names the
signature header, its prefix and the optional timestamp header and tolerance; the signed
message is `"{timestamp}.{body}"` for a timestamped provider and the raw body otherwise, signed
with HMAC-SHA256 under the signing secret the destination's credential holds. A delivery is
recorded as `email.delivered`, a bounce as `email.bounced` (with `kind` `hard` or `soft`) and a
complaint as `email.complained`. A hard bounce suppresses the address the message was sent to
in every workspace of the organization, a complaint in the destination's workspace only, and a
soft bounce nobody. A repeat of an event writes nothing.

parameters.description: The id of the provider destination, in the URL given to the provider

patch.summary:
Changes the workspace's settings: its time zone and its automatic UTM parameters. Needs the
workspace admin role and the CSRF token. Audited as `workspace.updated` for the time zone and
`workspace.utm_updated` for the UTM setting, in one transaction.

post.summary:
Drafts a mapping, a manifest, a segment, a flow or a template (`kind`: `mapping`, `manifest`,
`segment`, `flow` or `template`; a flow draft names its flow in `flow_id` and also returns a
`simulation` of a few synthetic people; a template draft names its template in `template_id`
and its `task` (`copy`, `subject_variants`, `block_layout` or `translation`) and also returns
`renders`, the template's draft and the result rendered for the sample person) with the
assistant: the model is asked, its answer validated
with the rules a save applies, and problems are fed back for at most `ai.max_repair_attempts`
repairs. The answer is the validated draft with its diff against the saved version and a dry
run, or the last problems. Only a validated draft can be accepted. Editors and above who are
signed in (a mapping or manifest draft reads a source, so it takes an admin); an API key is
refused. Every attempt is a gated model call: it counts against the
budget and the rate limit, and with the assistant off, nothing is read or sent. A reverse
proxy in front needs a read timeout of at least (1 + `ai.max_repair_attempts`) x 60 s + 30 s.
post.description:
Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (1 to 255 characters) to make a retry safe for 24 hours, so a
retry after a timeout does not spend the budget twice. While the first request runs, the same
key answers `409 idempotency_key_in_flight` with `Retry-After`; once it has stored a draft
(valid or not), the same key and body answer `409 idempotency_key_replayed` with the draft's id
and no body, as the draft may hold values from the workspace; the same key with another body
is `422 idempotency_key_reused`. The key belongs to the caller that sent it. A failed run
stores nothing and leaves the key free.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1 to 255 characters; makes a retry safe for 24 hours. A key first used for another request answers 422 `idempotency_key_reused`

201.description: The draft run: a validated draft with its changes and dry run, or the problems of the last attempt

402.description: The workspace's monthly AI budget is spent (`ai_budget_exceeded`); nothing was sent

403.description: Not an editor, not an admin for a mapping or manifest draft, or an API key (`ai_user_required`)

404.description: No such workspace, source or stream, or no access

409.description: The assistant is off (`ai_disabled`), the source does not use a manifest, or the template is archived (`template_archived`)

422.description: A request that breaks a rule, naming the field, such as a missing prompt, `sample_required` or `sample_not_supported`; for a template `ai_template_too_large` (the document is over 96 KiB) or `ai_template_unsupported` (not an email template, a block layout of a code email, or, without the personal-data opt-in, a `visible_if` too deep or too large to mask)

429.description: Too many AI calls (`ai_rate_limited`); try again in a minute

502.description: The model provider failed (`ai_provider_error`), the source did, or (a template draft) the render host answered unusably (`render_protocol`)

503.description: The server has no master key to open the provider key, or (a template draft) the render host stopped (`render_child_exited`) or rendering is not available (`render_unavailable`)

post.summary:
Accepts a draft of the signed-in user: checks that it is valid, that the saved version has not
changed since and that it still passes the rules a save applies, then returns it for the
editor to load as its unsaved draft. Nothing is written to the stream or the source; saving
stays a separate action. Audited as `ai.draft.accepted`. Editors and above who are signed in.

200.description: The draft, to load into the editor

403.description: Not an editor, not an admin for a mapping or manifest draft, or an API key (`ai_user_required`)

404.description: No such draft of this user in this workspace, or it expired

409.description: The draft never validated (`ai_draft_invalid`), the saved version changed since (`ai_draft_outdated`), the flow of a flow draft is archived (`flow_archived`), the template of a template draft is archived (`template_archived`), or its draft changed or was replaced since this draft was made (`template_draft_changed`)

422.description: The draft no longer passes the rules a save applies, such as a trait archived since (the same codes as a save; for a flow draft `flow_invalid` with the publish validation issues; for a template draft `template_invalid` with the publish validation issues)

post.summary:
Uploads an image. The body is the raw file with its own `Content-Type`: `image/png`,
`image/jpeg`, `image/gif` or `image/webp`; SVG and every other type are refused before the
body is read. The type must match the file's magic bytes. The file may be at most
`assets.max_file_bytes` (5 MiB by default) and 8192 pixels a side and 40 megapixels, read from
its header. The workspace's images may take at most `assets.max_workspace_bytes` together. The
same bytes uploaded again to the workspace return the existing asset with 200. Audited as
`asset.uploaded` with the id, name and size.
post.description:
Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (1 to 255 characters) to make a retry safe for 24 hours.
While the first request runs, the same key answers `409 idempotency_key_in_flight` with
`Retry-After`; once it has stored the image, the same key and file answer
`409 idempotency_key_replayed` with the asset's id and no body, as the name may be a
person's value; the same key with another file is `422 idempotency_key_reused`. The key
belongs to the caller that sent it.

get.summary:
Watches the workspace's events as they are decided: one `item` frame per outcome
(`accepted`, `flagged`, `unplanned`, `rejected` or `duplicate`), live, with no
history beyond the last few seconds before it connected (so a batch that was still
committing is not missed). Each frame's `id` is `<epoch>:<position>`, a position that is
safe to resume from: send it back as `Last-Event-ID` and the stream continues after it,
possibly repeating a few rows the client already has (their `seq` identifies them). A row
whose writer commits late is sent when it does, so frames may arrive out of order by `seq`;
a row that commits more than twice the 10 s patience after a later row was sent can still
be missed, and a resumed stream does not deliver a late row below its resume point whose
writer committed while the client was away. The epoch names the life of the feed, which is
unlogged and starts over after a crash: a position from another epoch, or an older bare
number, is answered with a `gap` frame whose `reset` is true, and the stream starts at the
current position; an open stream that notices the crash on its poll does the same. A viewer that
cannot keep up gets an `event: gap` frame with the number of rows skipped (an upper bound
when filters apply). While the server's notifier is down, an `event: status` frame says
`degraded` and the stream polls every few seconds instead of reacting at once; another says
it recovered.

kind.description:
`sync` (the default) or `reconcile`. A reconciliation needs `stream`, which must be
incremental.

stream.description: The name of one stream. Without it every enabled stream with a mapping is run.

node_type.description:
The node's type in the pinned version's graph (such as `wait.duration`); null for a node the
version does not have.

enabled.description: Whether runs read this stream. New streams start disabled.

oneOf.description: Whether the data is current; null while the stream, or its source, is disabled.
How a record of the stream becomes a person; null until one is set.

reconcile_schedule.description:
The UTC cron on which the stream is reconciled: its keys are listed and the live records the
source no longer has are removed. Null for none. Incremental streams only.

staleness_threshold_seconds.description:
The stream's own threshold: seconds without a successful run before the stream counts as
stale. Absent means twice the source schedule's interval, or never stale when the source
has no schedule. `freshness.threshold_seconds` is the one in force.

sweep_limit.description:
The largest share (above 0, at most 1) of the stream's live records that one sweep, after a
full refresh or a reconciliation, may remove. A run that would remove more removes nothing
and fails with `sweep_limit`. 1 turns the guard off.

cursor_field.description: A field of the stream. Required for `incremental`.

oneOf.description:
How a record of the stream becomes a person. Absent leaves the stream's mapping as it is.
Columns are the stream's field names (top level); trait keys must be in the registry.

primary_key.description: Fields of the stream that identify a record.

reconcile_schedule.description: A UTC cron to reconcile the stream on. Absent or null clears it. Incremental streams only.

sweep_limit.description:
The largest share of the stream's live records one sweep may remove: above 0, at most 1.
Absent resets it to the default, 0.5.

from.description: Start of the window, inclusive (UTC): midnight of the first day counted.

to.description: End of the window (UTC): the time of the request.

hash_prefix.description:
The first 8 hex characters of the identifier hash. The full hash and the value are
never returned here.

reason.description: `hard_bounce`, `complaint`, `manual` or `erased`.

source.description: Where it came from, such as `api`, `ui`, `import` or `erasure`.

added.description: Identifiers that were, or on a dry run would be, newly suppressed.

existing.description: Identifiers already suppressed, and repeats within the file.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null when there is none.

oneOf.description: An identifier: `email`, `phone`, `anonymous_id` or `external:<namespace>`.
A trait by registry key; it must exist and not be archived.
A truthy cell (`true`, `1`, `yes`, `x`, and so on) adds the person to the list.
The column is not used.

value.description: The identifier value. It is looked up and not stored.

category.description: `marketing` or `transactional`; fixed when the template is made.

channel.description: `email` or `webhook`; fixed when the template is made.

created_by.description: The user who created it; null when an API key did.

current_version.description: The newest published version; null before the first publish.

sender_identity_id.description:
The sender identity the draft's document names (`email.sender`), when it is an identity of
this workspace. Read-only: it follows the draft, which is where the sender is set.

utm.description:
`inherit` (the default) follows the workspace's UTM setting; `off` never adds UTM
parameters to this template's links.

TemplateCategoryRequest.description: Whether a message needs the unsubscribe link and headers.

TemplateChannelRequest.description: The channel of a template. Only the two with a registered content type can be made.

TemplateChecksBody.description: The counts of the issues the draft's last validation found.

TemplateDraftBody.description: The one editable copy of a template's content.

content_type.description: The registered content type that owns the document (`html`, `webhook`); null when none does.

document.description: The content document. It may be incomplete; only a publish validates it.

revision.description: How many times the draft has been saved; the first save is 1.

TemplateHeaderBody.description: A header of the rendered message or request.

TemplateIssueProblem.description: One issue of a template document.

at.description: A JSON pointer into the document.

code.description: A fixed issue code such as `unknown_merge_field` or `missing_unsubscribe`.

field.description: The merge field the issue concerns, such as `person.first_name`.

message.description: A short explanation for a problem the code alone does not explain.

active_flows.description: How many active flows send the template.

oneOf.description: The draft's last validation; null when it has not been checked.

draft_changed.description: The draft differs from the current version; false before the first publish.

edited_by_email.description: The email of the member who saved the draft last; null for an API key or a removed member.

TemplateListItemBody.description: A template in the library list: the template and the facts the library shows.

TemplateNamedTheme.description: A theme a block email names.

TemplatePreviewBody.description: The rendered template and its validation results.

content_type.description: The registered content type that rendered it (`html`, `webhook`).

headers.description: An email's extra headers (`List-Unsubscribe` for marketing mail) or a webhook's headers.

hidden_blocks.description: The sections and blocks this person does not see because their `visible_if` was false.

html.description: An email's HTML, with inert tracking links.

issues.description: The same checks a publish makes, against the workspace's fields now.

person_id.description:
The person whose values were used; null for the sample person. When the id asked for was
merged away, the survivor.

rendered.description: False when the document has blocking issues, so nothing was rendered.

annotate.description:
Give each section and block the class `zf-block-<id>` in the HTML, so a page can mark
them. Only the preview does this; a send, a test send and a publish never do.

person_id.description:
Preview as this person. Needs the workspace admin role, because the render shows their
values. Absent: a sample person built from the field registry's types.

version.description: Preview this published version. Absent: the draft.

TemplatePublishRequest.description: The optional body of a publish.

note.description: A note for the version history, at most 500 characters. Blank is no note.

revision.description:
The revision of the draft that was reviewed. When given, a draft saved since is a 409
`template_draft_changed` and nothing is published.

TemplatePublishedBody.description: The new version and the template after the publish.

used_by.description: The active flows that send this template, which now send the new version.

TemplateRendersBody.description: A template draft before and after the change, both rendered for the sample person.

oneOf.description: The drafted document.
The template's draft as it is now; absent when it has blocking issues and does not render.

TemplateSendVolumeBody.description: How much one active flow sends the template.

per_day.description: The average non-test messages a day over the last 7 days.

TemplateTask.description: What the marketer asks the assistant to do to a template.

TemplateThemeBody.description: The theme the draft follows: `default`, `none`, or the theme it names.

TemplateThemeChoice.description: A theme choice that names no theme row.

TemplateUseBody.description: One flow with a version that names the template.

active.description: Whether the version the flow runs now is one of them.

versions.description:
The numbers of the flow's versions that name the template, newest first. An older version
still runs for the enrollments pinned to it.

TemplateUtmRequest.description: The per-template override of the workspace UTM setting.

document.description: The document as it was published.

note.description: The note written when it was published.

warnings.description: The warnings found when it was published; a blocking issue refuses the publish.

messages.description: The non-test messages sent with the version.

more.description: Whether more combinations exist than `renders` lists.

renders.description: The distinct theme and snippet combinations, most used first, at most 20.

TemplateVersionSummaryBody.description: One published version in the history list: no document, which `GET .../versions/{n}` returns.

blocking.description:
The blocking issues stored with the version; always 0, because a blocking issue refuses the
publish.

note.description: The note written when it was published.

warnings.description: The warnings stored with the version.

error.description: Why it does not. Never holds a credential or a URL.

TestCredentialRequest.description: Which source or destination runs the check. Exactly one id.

destination_id.description: A destination that uses this credential.

source_id.description: A source that uses this credential.

TestSendBody.description: A test send as the log shows it. It holds no address, no hash and no person.

draft_revision.description: The draft revision a draft test rendered; null for a version test.

id.description: Also the idempotency key at the destination.

member_id.description: The user who asked; null for an API key.

reason.description: A fixed code that says why a test did not go out.

recipient_display.description:
A member's email, or the hint of the allowlist entry the test went to; `removed address`
once the entry is gone. Never an allowlisted address.

recipient_member_id.description: The workspace member the test went to; null for an allowlisted address.

render_context.description: `person` when a person's values rendered the template, else `sample`.

sent_by_email.description: The email of the member who asked; null for an API key or a removed member.

template_version.description: The published version sent; null for the draft.

TestSendRecipient.description: Who a test goes to. Exactly one of the three fields is given.

address.description: An address on the workspace's test-send allowlist.

allowlist_entry.description: An entry of the allowlist, by the id the allowlist options list. The address stays sealed.

member.description: A member of this workspace; the test goes to the address on their account.

destination_id.description: The destination to send through, as a send node names it.

person_id.description:
Render with this person's values; needs the workspace admin role, as a preview does.
Absent: the sample person. The person is not recorded in the log.

sender_identity_id.description:
The sender identity, as a send node names it. It must be live on a verified domain, or the
test ends `sender_unverified`.

version.description: The published version to send. Absent: the current draft.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null when there is none.

created_by.description: The user who created it; null when an API key did.

current_version.description: The newest published version; null before the first publish.

is_default.description: Whether emails that follow the default theme use this one.

ThemeDraftBody.description: The one editable copy of a theme's tokens.

revision.description:
How many times the draft has been saved; the first save is 1. Send it back as `revision`
to save only if nobody saved in between.

tokens.description: The tokens. They may fail the publish checks; only a publish validates them fully.

ThemeFlowBody.description: An active flow that sends a template that uses the theme.

template_ids.description: The templates of the flow that use the theme.

tokens.description: The current version's tokens, or the draft's while the theme has never been published.

used_by_templates.description:
How many templates, not archived, use the theme: their draft or current version names it,
and, for the default theme, they follow the default.

ThemeListItemBody.description: A theme in the list, with what a card shows.

ThemePreviewBody.description: The rendered sample and the theme's validation results.

html.description: The sample document's HTML, with inert tracking links.

issues.description:
The checks a publish makes. A logo or footer that cannot be used is a warning here: the
preview shows a stand-in logo or no footer.

rendered.description: False when the tokens have blocking issues, so nothing was rendered.

version.description: Preview this published version. Absent: the draft.

ThemePublishedBody.description: The new version, the theme after the publish, and what uses the theme.

used_by.description: What picks the new version up: later renders use it without a template being republished.

ThemeTemplateBody.description: A template whose draft or current version uses the theme.

in_current.description: Whether the template's current version uses the theme.

in_draft.description: Whether the template's draft uses the theme.

active_flows.description:
Flows whose running version names a template of either list. A flow that does not run it
now, and an archived flow, is not listed.

default_templates.description:
Block templates, not archived, whose draft or current version follows the workspace
default (`theme` absent or `"default"`). Empty unless this theme is the default.

named_templates.description: Templates, not archived, whose draft or current version names the theme.

tokens.description: The tokens as they were published.

warnings.description: The warnings found when it was published; a blocking issue refuses the publish.

ThemeVersionSummaryBody.description: One published version in the history list: no tokens, which `GET .../versions/{n}` returns.

warnings.description: The warnings stored with the version.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null when there is none.

key.description: Lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens; unique in the workspace.

policy.description: `opt_in`: allowed only when subscribed. `opt_out`: allowed unless unsubscribed.

trace_id.description: The trace id: 32 lowercase hex characters.

truncated.description: True when the trace has more records than this response carries.

identifiers.description:
Identifier kind to value. At least one of `userId`, `anonymousId` and `identifiers`
is required.

messageId.description: 1 to 200 characters. Resending the same `messageId` stores the event once.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 time the event occurred; the arrival time when absent.

index_state.description:
Set while the trait holds a typed slot: `backfilling`, `ready` (segments read the column) or
`retiring`. Null for a trait stored only as JSON.

inferred.description: Registered automatically from an incoming record rather than created by a person.

source_order.description: Source names in priority order; used by `source_priority`.

TraitQuery.description:
A trait to compare. The operators that apply depend on the trait's registry type: `eq`
and `exists` for any type (a `string_list` matches when it holds the value), `prefix` for
strings, and `gt`, `gte`, `lt` and `lte` for numbers, timestamps and dates.

value.description: Required for every operator but `exists`; it must fit the trait's type.

oneOf.description: Converts the text to a type.

Parses a date or time into a UTC timestamp. `format` is a strftime pattern such as
`%d/%m/%Y %H:%M`, or `unix` or `unix_ms`.
Joins the value with other columns' values, skipping empty ones.
Ignores the cell and uses this text.
Replaces a value that is a key of the map; others stay as they are.
Splits the text into a list of trimmed, non-empty strings.

TransformBody.description: One step between a cell and its target.

UnhealthyInputBody.description: A source that feeds what the flow reads and is not fresh.

last_success_at.description: When its oldest feeding stream last succeeded; null when one never has.

state.description: `stale` or `failing`: the worst state among the source's enabled streams.

reason.description: `not_found`, `malformed_row`, or the rule the identifier broke, such as `invalid_email`.

row.description:
The line of the file the row starts on, counting the header as line 1. A quoted value
that spans lines moves later rows down, as an editor shows them.

fields.description: Replaces the whole object of non-secret values.

credential_id.description: Uses another workspace credential, which must hold every required credential field.

retention_days.description:
Days events of this name are kept, within the operator's bounds; `null` goes back to
the deployment default.

cadence_minutes.description: How often a time-sensitive segment is recomputed in full, in minutes; default 60.

from_address.description: An address on the identity's domain.

reply_to.description: A new reply-to address; `null` clears it.

credential_id.description: Uses another workspace credential, which must hold every required credential field.

schedule.description: A cron expression in UTC; an empty string clears the schedule.

oneOf.description:
`inherit` or `off`: whether the workspace's automatic UTM parameters apply to this
template.

enabled.description: Stops or resumes receiving without losing the setup.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone name such as `Europe/Copenhagen` or `UTC`, at most 64 characters.

oneOf.description: The automatic UTM parameter setting, replaced as a whole.

UsedByBody.description: A live source or destination that uses a credential.

UserBody.description: A user as shown to API callers; never includes the password hash.

user_id.description: Null for calls made with an API key.

UtmSettingsBody.description:
The workspace setting for automatic UTM parameters on email links. A pattern may use only
`{workspace}`, `{flow}`, `{flow_version}`, `{step}`, `{template}`, `{template_version}` and
`{category}`; values are slugged and URL-encoded, and a pattern that expands to nothing omits
its parameter.

domains.description: The link domains that get parameters; their subdomains do too. Enabling needs at least one.

oneOf.description:
The credential schema the manifest declares in `auth.credential` (a built-in kind it names,
or its own fields), so the credential form can be drawn from it; null when it declares
none or the manifest is invalid. Create the credential as kind `custom` with this schema.

issues.description: At most 50, in the order found; empty when the manifest is valid.

streams.description: The streams the manifest declares, for a stream picker; empty when it is invalid.

manifest.description: The draft manifest: any JSON value. Whether it is a valid manifest v1 is the answer.

valid.description: True exactly when there are no issues: the flow can be published.

value.description: The property's text; a list or an object is its JSON.

ValueRuleBody.description: A column and the transforms that turn it into a value.

nodes.description:
The nodes of the version's graph in their order, then `settings.goal` when the version has
a goal setting. A node with no rows has zeros.

VersionRenderBody.description: One theme and snippet combination recorded on the messages sent with a version.

count.description: The non-test messages with this combination.

snippet_versions.description: Snippet id to the version number used.

theme_id.description: The theme in effect, or none.

WaitBody.description: A wait the walk went into.

awaiting.description: The event name a `wait.until_event` waits for.

resolved.description: `open`, `timer`, `event`, `timeout`, or `exit` (the flow settings ended the enrollment).

wake_at.description: The time the timer fires (the timeout, for `wait.until_event`).

WakeBody.description: A timer the engine asked for.

fired.description: Whether the walk reached `at` and fired it.

key.description: The unique key of the `flow.step` job the runtime would enqueue.

accepted.description: Payloads appended to the inbox: always 1. They are durable, not yet applied.

WebhookBody.description: A hook as the API shows it. Never holds the secret.

dedupe_field.description:
The path in the payload whose value identifies it; a replay of the same value is
recognised.

name.description: The source's name.

path.description: The path to send payloads to, relative to the server's origin.

receiving.description: Whether the hook accepts payloads: the source and the stream are enabled and mapped.

timestamp_header.description:
The header holding the unix seconds the sender signed; null for a hook that signs the
body alone.

editable.description: Whether this API changes the window for a workspace admin.

oneOf.description: The last run of the job that enforces the window; null before its first run.

max.description: The longest window allowed; null when there is no upper bound.

min.description: The shortest window allowed; null when there is no lower bound.

source.description: `workspace` when this workspace's own setting applies, else `deployment`.

value.description: The effective window; null when the assistant stores no transcripts.

timezone.description:
The workspace's IANA time zone, the local clock of a wait for a person with no zone of
their own. `UTC` until an admin sets it.

utm.description: The automatic UTM parameter setting for email links. Off until an admin turns it on.

computed_at.description:
When the rollup last finished a run. The counts lag the data by up to about seven
minutes (five between runs and a two minute commit margin); a workspace the rollup has
not reached yet shows zeros and the time of the request.

events_received.description: Events received in the window. Null for a caller who may not read events.

messages_sent.description: Messages that ended `sent` in the window; test sends excluded.

api_key.description: Workspace API key (zfk_...). Valid only for its own workspace and within its scopes.

session.name: zf_session
session.description: Session cookie set by POST /api/v1/session. Every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE              made with it must also send the CSRF token in the x-csrf-token header.
